content.title: Malcolm in the Middle creator on why having non-binary sibling in reboot was 'so important'
content.text: Published 17:24 10 Apr 2026 GMT+1Malcolm's younger sibling is non-binary and uses they/them pronouns in the reboot20 years on from Malcolm in the Middle Malcolm, Hal, Lois, Reese, and the whole family are back for the new four-episode reboot special.Whilst Erik Per Sullivan turned down ‘bucket loads of money’ to appear in the series, having retired from Hollywood and acting altogether, the rest of the main cast are all back for the special, including star Frankie Muniz.Reboots cannot simply live off of nostalgia however so it was natural that Malcolm in the Middle: Life’s Still Unfair would introduce some brand-new characters.Alongside Malcolm’s daughter Leah, there is one new character who actually technically did appear in the original TV show.Malcolm’s sibling Kelly is introduced in the show, with Lois having learned she was pregnant with a sixth child, but appear properly for the first time in the reboot.Kelly is non-binary, meaning that they do not identify as either of the binary gender of male or female.Kelly is revealed to be non-binary in the reboot (Disney+)Though Hal struggles in the show Kelly predominantly uses they/them pronouns, and the decision to have their youngest child be non-binary was one that the show’s creator did for a very specific reason, saying it was ‘so important’.The show’s creator Linwood Boomer and his wife, executive producer Tracy Katsy, spoke to Deadline about the reboot.Katsy was asked specifically about Kelly, saying in response: “I gotta tell you, it’s a really important thing to us.“Three out of four of our kids are queer, and without making it a thing and without making an issue, I think it’s really nice to have a character that, that’s just a facet of their personality as opposed to the entire story.Malcolm in the Middle reboot trailerCredit: Hulu0 seconds of 1 minute, 36 secondsVolume 90%Press shift question mark to access a list of keyboard shortcutsKeyboard ShortcutsShortcuts that’s really happening around me.”Kelly is not the only LGBTQIA+ representation in the series either, with returning character Stevie being portrayed as being gay and with his own family.The reboot has been largely given positive reviews, sitting at a score of 81% on Rotten Tomatoes.Robert Lloyd of the Los Angeles Times gave the show a positive review, saying that ‘it’s true to itself’.Cristina Escobar of RogerEbert.com gave the show 3.5/4 stars, saying: “It is loud, uncouth, heartfelt, uneven, and hilarious.“It carries on the tradition of the original that way. And like the original, it’s worth a watch.”Malcolm in the Middle: Life’s Still Unfair is available to stream on Disney+ nowFeatured Image Credit: Disney+Topics: TV, Nostalgia, TV and Film, LGBTQMichael SlavinMichael Slavin is LADbible's dedicated specialist Film and TV writer. 11:48 14 Apr 2026 GMT+1Malcolm in the Middle reboot hints at iconic trio 'throuple' in surprising sceneThe Krelybones are revealed to have a child together in the reboot Malcolm in the Middle: Life's Still UnfairMalcolm in the Middle: Life’s Still Unfair brings back the iconic TV family in all their glory, with all of the siblings brought back along with Hal and Lois.This even included the child that Hal and Lois discover they are having at the end of the show, Kelly, who is now Malcolm’s youngest sibling and is revealed to be non-binary.Malcolm in the Middle was not solely made up of the family though, with the beloved TV series also bringing back some of the other side characters that made the show so beloved.Amongst these is Stevie, Malcolm’s best friend from the original series, who is revealed to be gay and happily married with a son.Stevie is one of the Krelboynes, a group of gifted students (with less than perfect social capabilities) who Malcolm is friends with.Of the other Krelboynes there are three major characters who appear in the majority of the show: Dabney, Kevin, and Lloyd.The Krelyboynes were a major part of the original show, especially the first few seasons (Disney+)Of all the options for what the trio would be up to there are a huge host of possibilities for what the formerly geeky clique would now be doing, but very few fans could have predicted the real answer.Malcolm runs into the Krelboynes at Lois and Hal’s engagement party and, despite trying to pretend he doesn’t know them, is dragged over by Malcolm’s girlfriend Tristan.Dabney lets Malcom know they’ve missed their ‘fourth musketeer’ before revealing that the trio have ‘created a child’ together.Their kid is called ‘Hubert’, and when asked whether they used a surrogate they simply respond ‘sure’.One fan posted a picture of the Krelyboynes, with a viral quote tweet saying: “the top three being in a polycule is honestly the funniest bit of the revival.” Another fan responded questioning whether the possible platonic throuple ‘are a polycule because they love each other’ or whether they’re too afraid to talk to other people, adding: “I need a special episode showing their dynamic because it must be chaos with a kid in the middle of it all.”Whilst many fans on social media are split on if they are in a throuple together, the one thing that everyone appears to be in agreement on is that Hubert is a test tube made by the Krelyboynes trio.They are revealed to be working for ‘GenetiTech Resources’, stating they are doing ‘so much weird sh*t’.One fan said on Reddit: “I still have no idea what the deal with the Krelboynes is? Are they all gay and together? What's the deal with that kid? Is he some kind of a science project?”Is Hubert a test tube baby? A clone? Some child they stole from a hospital? Who knows. (Disney+)Whilst not everyone agreed, one popular comment said: “Their weird science sh*t involved mixing all their DNA to create a kid.”Until we get a finalised answer of whether it’s a platonic throuple, a full on polycule, or an accidental throuple they’re unaware they are in with their test tube baby, it’s just good to see the iconic characters together on screen again.Malcolm in the Middle: Life’s Still Unfair is available to stream on Disney+ now.Featured Image Credit: Disney+Topics: TV, Nostalgia, TV and Film, LGBTQMichael SlavinMichael Slavin is LADbible's dedicated specialist Film and TV writer.
